title: Autocommands and Commands
description: React to events: yank highlights, filetype settings, trim on save, and augroups that survive re-sourcing.

intro: An autocommand runs code when something happens: a file is opened or saved, its filetype is set, a yank finishes. vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd(event, { pattern = ..., callback = ... }) creates one.
Put them in an augroup created with clear = true. Then sourcing your config again replaces them, instead of adding a second copy of each.

commands.text: The event right after a yank.
Briefly highlights the text just yanked, when called from a TextYankPost callback. Before Neovim 0.11 it was vim.highlight.on_yank.
The event when a buffer's filetype is set. Its pattern is the filetype's name, such as markdown, not the file extension.
The event just before a buffer is written, the moment to trim whitespace. BufWritePost comes after the write.
vim.api.nvim_create_augroup(name, { clear = true }) groups autocommands, and deletes the old ones each time it runs.

levels.title: Flash the yank
levels.hint: vim.hl.on_yank() does the highlighting. Call it from the callback.

levels.title: What's in a name
levels.description: Markdown files should get spell checking, but the autocommand never fires.
levels.hint: FileType patterns match the filetype's name, not the file extension. :set filetype? in a .md file says markdown.

levels.title: Trim on save
levels.description: Trailing whitespace should be gone from the file you save, but it only disappears after saving, leaving the buffer modified.

probes.description: :w saves the trimmed text to disk

levels.hint: BufWritePost runs after the write; BufWritePre runs before it.

levels.title: Source it twice
levels.description: Re-sourcing this config adds a second copy of the autocommand every time. Make it idempotent.
levels.hint: An augroup created with clear = true deletes its old autocommands, so re-sourcing replaces them.
